stories.title: Nominal yields are high but the term premium remains low; real yields are the larger driver.
stories.whatChanged: 10Y nominal ~5% with 10Y real ~2.66% and NY Fed ACM term premium ~0.67% (5‑session -8.3bp), indicating real‑rate/policy repricing rather than a large term‑premium spike.
stories.whyItMatters: If yields reflect higher real policy expectations rather than term‑premium, credit and volatility transmission is less mechanically guaranteed but still possible if persistence continues.
stories.mechanism: Policy/repricing and higher real yields lift nominal yields; governed term‑premium is low so the long‑end move currently tracks real/policy repricing rather than a structural term‑premium shock.
stories.conclusion: Rates pressure is primarily a real‑rate/policy repricing story today, with a low ACM term premium that does not yet indicate a structural long‑end term‑premium shock.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Evidence of a sustained rise in the ACM term premium, a persistent unexplained nominal‑real gap, or repeated weak long‑end auction metrics would shift this to a term‑premium/structure problem.

stories.title: High‑yield spreads have widened materially more than IG over the trailing 20 sessions.
stories.whatChanged: 20‑session HY OAS change ~+45bp versus IG ~+10bp, signalling concentrated stress in lower‑credit tiers over the measurement window.
stories.whyItMatters: HY widening outpacing IG can precede broader credit transmission if sustained, but current IG moves are modest and volatility evidence (MOVE/VIX) is missing.
stories.mechanism: Either issuer/sector idiosyncratic weakness concentrated in HY or an early stage of rates‑driven credit repricing that has not yet materially widened IG spreads.
stories.conclusion: Credit weakness is currently concentrated in HY; IG shows only modest widening so broad credit stress is not confirmed.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Persistent multi‑session IG OAS widening and a canonical MOVE/VIX spike would indicate broadening credit stress.

stories.title: Large‑cap breadth is healthy while AI/semiconductor breadth is mixed and semis lag relative to Nasdaq.
stories.whatChanged: Large‑cap breadth >50‑day and 200‑day averages; AI basket breadth positive vs 50d but weak vs 50d and many AI names at 20‑day lows; SMH underperformance vs QQQ over 20 sessions.
stories.whyItMatters: Broad large‑cap strength cushions markets from rates pressure, but concentrated weakness in AI/infra would matter if it spread to broader small‑cap or credit channels.
stories.mechanism: Market leadership remains concentrated (Magnificent Seven/large caps), while the tracked AI basket shows thinner internals, implying an uneven risk‑appetite landscape.
stories.conclusion: Breadth is mixed: large caps are broadly healthy while AI/semiconductor internals are weaker, leaving market leadership concentrated.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: A sustained deterioration in large‑cap breadth or a reversal where SMH materially underperforms QQQ across sessions would indicate broader equity weakness.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.
